"Implement the solution in src/lib.rs so that the tests in tests/luhn-from.rs pass. The specification follows.

# Luhn: Using the From Trait

Before doing this exercise you should probably do the original Luhn exercise. If you have not completed Luhn, you can get it by running the command:

```shell
exercism download --exercise=luhn --track=rust
```

In the original Luhn exercise you only validated strings, but the Luhn algorithm can be applied to integers as well.

In this exercise you'll implement the [From trait](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/convert/trait.From.html) to convert strings, strs and unsigned integers into a Struct that performs the validation.


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper modules may go under src/; you may add [dependencies] from the offline crates listed in OFFLINE_CRATES.md to Cargo.toml."

Everything works. The solution is complete. Let me summarize.

The solution:
- Stores the input as a `String` in the `Luhn` struct.
- `is_valid()` implements the Luhn algorithm: strips whitespace, rejects non-digit characters, requires at least 2 digits, doubles every second digit from the right (subtracting 9 if > 9), and checks the sum is divisible by 10.
- Uses a single generic `impl<T: ToString> From<T> for Luhn` which covers `&str`, `String`, and all unsigned integer types — this is the "better solution" the hint was pointing to, avoiding hand-writing each `From` impl.

No new files, no dependency changes needed. Done.

Done. All tests pass.

## What I did

Implemented the solution entirely in `src/lib.rs` (no new files, no dependency changes needed):

1. **`Luhn` struct** now stores the input as a `String`.

2. **`is_valid()`** implements the Luhn algorithm:
   - Walks the characters, collecting ASCII digit values; any character that is neither a digit nor whitespace makes the input invalid.
   - Rejects inputs with fewer than two digits (so `"0"` and `"1"` are invalid).
   - Doubles every second digit counting from the rightmost, subtracting 9 when the result exceeds 9.
   - Returns true when the sum is divisible by 10.

3. **`From` trait** — instead of hand-writing a `From` impl for each type (which the stub hint warned "will fail if a new type is presented"), I used a single generic implementation:
   ```rust
   impl<T: ToString> From<T> for Luhn {
       fn from(input: T) -> Self {
           Luhn { input: input.to_string() }
       }
   }
   ```
   Since `&str`, `String`, and every unsigned integer type implement `Display` (and thus `ToString`), this one impl covers all of them — and any future type that can be rendered as a string.

- `cargo test --test luhn-from -- --include-ignored` → **14 passed, 0 failed**
- Default `cargo test` → clean (1 passed, 13 ignored per the `#[ignore]` annotations)
